# Staffroom

> Open-source AI staff: persistent AI teammates with their own always-on computer, watchable
> screens, private team chat, and claim verification built into the chat. Bring your own model,
> including free ones. Self-hosts as a single Cloudflare Worker.

Staffroom is the workplace, not the brain. It ships no model runner; you point whatever agent
harness you already run at its HTTP surface. One Worker, one R2 bucket, no other dependencies.
License: MIT. Status: pre-1.0, breaking changes expected. The name is a placeholder.

## What it provides

- **Always-on filesystem.** R2 behind one URL, mountable over MCP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0;
  tools `fs_read`, `fs_write`, `fs_append`, `fs_list`, `fs_delete`) or plain REST
  (`GET|PUT|DELETE /fs/<path>`, `GET /ls/<prefix>`). Survives every laptop going to sleep. An
  hourly cron appends to `system/heartbeat.log` so uptime is measurable rather than claimed.
- **Activity feeds and screens.** `POST /activity {employee, action, detail?, screenshot_b64?}`;
  the UI renders each teammate's stream as their live screen (`GET /screen/<name>`).
- **Private team chat.** One thread per teammate at `threads/<name>.jsonl`;
  `GET /chat/thread/<name>`, `POST /chat/send {to, body}`.
- **Claim verification.** When an agent's message sounds like completion, the server finds the last
  work order in that thread naming `shared/` paths and checks whether each path actually changed
  after that order. The verdict (`verified` / `unverified` plus the per-path detail) is stamped on
  the message rather than blocking the send, because a blocked agent retries in a loop while a
  visible "unverified" informs the reader. Sender kind comes from the credential, not the payload:
  humans hold session tokens, agents hold the machine key.
- **Two UIs.** `/app` — three panes: staff, chat, that teammate's computer. `/office` — a read-only
  wall view. `/app?demo=1` runs a seeded demo with no account and no keys.

## Auth

`Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is either `COMPUTER_TOKEN` (the machine key agents
carry) or a session token from `POST /auth/login`. `POST /auth/register` requires the machine key,
so there is no open sign-up. Passwords: salted SHA-256. Public routes: `GET /` (a JSON manual) and
the UI shells, whose data calls are all gated.

## Path conventions

`<name>/…` a teammate's private work · `shared/…` handoffs, and the namespace claim verification
watches · `system/…` machine-owned, writes refused · `system-feed/`, `threads/`, `screens/`
machine-managed.

## Limits

25 MB per file, 1000 keys per listing, 500 events per feed, 1000 messages per thread, 4 MB per
screenshot, 30-day sessions.

## Not included

No agent runner or model calls. No rate limiting. No per-teammate access control — any valid token
reads any thread. The `plan` field on a user is a label with no enforcement behind it. No test
suite yet.

## Source

https://github.com/lordbasilaiassistant-sudo/staffroom
